children: Optical networking stocks climbed in premarket trading Friday as a shortage of components used in artificial intelligence infrastructure drew investor attention.
advanced around 5% alongside other suppliers after industry commentary pointed to limited production capacity extending into 2029.

Lumentum's chief executive said the company's available supply had been committed through early 2029. The situation reflects the challenge manufacturers face in keeping up with technology companies expanding their data center networks to support increasingly demanding AI workloads.

The supply crunch could create opportunities for competing manufacturers, including Fabrinet (FN), which provides manufacturing services for optical communications equipment. However, companies may need additional production capacity to capture more business, and expanding operations can involve higher costs and execution challenges.

For investors, the key question is whether current demand can support sustained financial growth. A lengthy order backlog provides visibility into customer requirements, but it does not guarantee that every supplier will achieve higher margins or convert orders into revenue on schedule. Production capacity, delivery performance and customer spending will remain important factors in determining how the sector performs.

title: Lumentum, Coherent Stocks Jump After CEO Warns AI Components Sold Out Through 2029
